source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Engine - Engine Tune Up, p.6-2

procedures.title: Compression test
steps: Crank the engine through at least 4 compression strokes to get the highest reading.
Check and write down the compression of every cylinder.
If any cylinders are low or uneven, squirt about a tablespoon of engine oil onto the pistons of the low cylinders through the plug hole, crank several times and test again.
If compression rises but not necessarily to normal, the rings are worn.
If compression does not rise, the valves are burned, sticking or not seating.
If two neighboring cylinders are low and oil does not help, suspect a head gasket leak between them (coolant and/or oil in the cylinders can result).
notes: CAUTION: whenever the engine is cranked remotely at the starter (jumper cable or other means), disconnect the primary distributor lead from the coil negative post and have the ignition switch ON; otherwise the grounding circuit in the ignition switch will be damaged.
If the compression test does not find a weak cylinder, use the Cylinder Balance Test under Additional Checks and Adjustments.

procedures.title: Spark plugs: service and install
steps: Inspect each plug for badly worn electrodes and glazed, broken or blistered porcelain; replace as needed (Section 6Y covers reading plug conditions).
Clean usable plugs well with an abrasive cleaner such as sand blast, and file the center electrode flat.
Check each plug's make and heat range; all plugs must be the same make and number.
Set the gaps to specification with a round feeler gauge, bending only the side (ground) electrode, never the center one (see figure 2 in the manual).
Test the plugs on a plug tester if one is available.

Inspect and clean the plug hole threads before installing; remove corrosion with a 14 mm x 1.25 SAE spark plug tap (from local jobbers) or a small wire brush in an electric drill, with grease on the tap to catch chips.
